summary: In the construct, racks of weapons appear and begin to arm themselves. Trinity observes that no one has ever attempted such a thing. Neo. answers with a terse "Yeah?", then snap-cocks an Uzi and declares that this is why it's going to work.

what_changes.before: He responds minimally to Trinity's awe with a terse "Yeah?"
what_changes.after: He commits to the plan, asserting "That's why it's going to work" as he arms himself.
what_changes.evidence: He snap-cocks an Uzi. NEO (CONT'D) That's why it's going to work.

event_hint.one_line: Neo and Trinity arm themselves in the construct ahead of a raid, with Neo confident because no one has ever done this before.

minds.wants: To convert Trinity's awe into shared confidence — to answer her disbelief not with reassurance but with the claim that their unprecedented move is precisely the weapon.
minds.feels: A hard, newly arrived certainty. The man who needed to be told he was The One is now the one setting the terms of an impossible plan, and the unfamiliarity of it is feeding him rather than frightening him.
minds.shows: A terse "Yeah?" that refuses to meet her wonder, then the physical punctuation of snap-cocking the Uzi and the flat declaration "That's why it's going to work." Compressed, almost offhand.
minds.basis: His 'Yeah?' deflects rather than joins Trinity's marvel; the facts note he moves from minimal response to asserting 'That's why it's going to work' while arming himself. His terse tone contrasts with the grandeur of Trinity's line, and the gun-cocking is a physical substitute for an argument.

believes_about.belief: That her astonishment is a gap he needs to close, that she hasn't yet seen what he now sees — that the rules have changed because he has.
believes_about.wrong_because: She isn't skeptical of the plan; she's in genuine awe of him. He reads her wonder as doubt to be overcome when it is closer to faith already arriving.

believes_about.belief: That she still sees him as the doubtful newcomer she was wary of on the Nebuchadnezzar.
believes_about.wrong_because: Her 'No one has ever pulled off something like this.' is spoken in a register of reverence, not caution. He is outrunning his own old self-image.

minds.wants: To name the magnitude of what's happening — less a question than a reckoning spoken aloud, marking that they are about to do something the world has no precedent for.
minds.feels: Awe edged with the vertigo of a warrior confronting the fact that the man beside her operates beyond every rule she has survived by. It is not fear of the mission; it is the shock of witnessing him become what Morpheus claimed he was.
minds.shows: A single quiet declarative line, offered rather than asked. She keeps her voice level and lets the statement stand — she doesn't gush, doesn't look at him for confirmation.
minds.basis: Her line 'She declares that no one has ever accomplished such a feat.' is a declaration, not a question, and it precedes his deflection; the facts frame her as observing with awe while Neo answers minimally. Earlier, on the Nebuchadnezzar, she doubted Neo outright, so her wonder here measures how far he has moved.

believes_about.belief: That his 'Yeah?' is a guard thrown up because he doesn't yet fully believe in himself and is uncomfortable with being the object of awe.
believes_about.wrong_because: His terseness is not discomfort but compression — he has already committed and is moving on to action. She may still be reading the old uncertainty into a man who has just outgrown it.

connects_back: sc-150: Neo's 'Guns. Lots of guns' call to Tank begins the arming this scene completes, and his terseness carries over into the 'Yeah?'
sc-151: Their bodies hanging motionless in the drive chairs — this is the interior, willed counterpart to that physical passivity, the mind loading what the body cannot yet do
Earlier-Neo's doubt on the Nebuchadnezzar: Trinity's awe only registers because we have seen her skepticism, and Neo's confidence only lands because we have seen his uncertainty
sets_up: ev-027: The assault on the government building — the unprecedented, rule-breaking tactics Trinity marvels at are exactly what they execute in the lobby, elevator, and rooftop firefight
ev-028: The helicopter rescue of Morpheus, where Neo's.50-caliber assault on Agents and Marines is the fullest expression of 'no one has ever done [.]'
ev-030: Trinity's confession of love in the subway booth — her awe here is the emotional substrate that later lets that confession arrive
dramatic_function: To transfer the scene's emotional weight onto Neo's transformed certainty: it converts the wonder of the impossible into a motive for the raid, and marks — quietly, in two lines and a cocked gun — that the doubter has become the believer, so that the crew's most reckless plan now has its surest voice.
